headline: CISA lists a patched Apple auth bypass as exploited, as a Zyxel zero-day's toll nears 1,000 switches
standfirst: A medium-severity Apple authentication bypass joins the federal exploited list, a Russia-linked watering-hole operation turns mobile exploit chains on Ukraine and its partners, and two trust-dependent vendors disclose breaches. Plus an AI exploit pipeline, a cold-chain warning and an OpenSSH bypass.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added CVE-2024-27834 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation — the day's only enriched CVE, and a MEDIUM at 5.5 [[s31]]. The national vulnerability database describes an improper-authentication (CWE-287) issue letting an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability bypass Pointer Authentication; the vector requires local access and low privileges, with no user interaction. Fixes shipped in Safari 17.5, iOS and iPadOS 16.7.8 and 17.5, macOS Sonoma 14.5, tvOS 17.5 and watchOS 10.5. The excerpt credits the flaw with delivering info-stealing malware but is truncated, and CISA's remediation deadline binds federal agencies, not everyone.

Separately, a Russia-linked watering-hole campaign is using mobile exploit chains against iOS and Android devices, aimed at entities in the US and Europe and mainly Ukraine [[s23]]. Analysis: the two stories share a theme — device-level exploitation as an entry point — but the Apple vector needs local access and nothing supplied links them. The campaign's attribution is the reporting's; its exploit details were not supplied.

Zyxel patched a GS1900 series switch zero-day that attackers had used to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide and steal configuration files and credentials [[s38]]. No CVE was supplied, so the identifier and fixed firmware range are unconfirmed here.

## Breaches

Chainalysis said some information belonging to all of its users was exposed in a cyberattack; its customers reportedly include law enforcement and national security bodies, and the reporting labels the techniques "agentic" without supplied detail on what that means [[s33]]. DigiCert traced its breach to a server migration that mistakenly exposed an internal business system to the internet, allowing access to customer information and identity documents [[s9]]. Analysis: for a certificate authority, leaked identity documents matter more than email addresses — they feed impersonation and account-recovery fraud — though no misuse is reported in the supplied text.

## Research

OpenAI detailed a prototype pipeline that analysed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724, and validated and patched 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities for $1.2 million in API costs [[s17]]. These are prototype results, not a shipped product; upstream reporting of the fixes is not in the excerpt.

## Industry

CISA, the FBI and the health, agriculture and transport departments said they are aware of malicious activity against industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems worldwide [[s19]]. No actor, motive or CVE accompanies the warning in the supplied text. Analysis: the value is in the asset class it names — internet-reachable cold-storage monitoring — not in technical detail, which was not supplied.

## Vulnerabilities

A newly disclosed OpenSSH flaw dubbed "*sshole" lets attackers log into certain Alpine Linux and other musl-based accounts that block password authentication, by entering an oversized password [[s2]]. Affected versions, a CVE and patch status were not supplied; container and Alpine hosts are the stated exposure.
